conventions.convention: Groups are supplied in explicit invariant-factor coordinates; the empty product is the trivial group. Coordinate residues use fixed-width big-endian encoding, concatenated in coordinate order, for both group elements and character labels.
The hiding promise is F(g)=F(g′) iff g−g′ belongs to H. The output encoding is injective, and the XOR oracle acts on a declared total Boolean extension, including invalid group codes.
The exact supplied QFT uses coefficients N^(−1/2) times the conjugate of χ(g), and is a unitary on the full encoded register. Preparation and QFT availability and efficiency are input assumptions.
Recovery outputs character constraints denoting their common kernel; the empty constraint list denotes G. Success means that this constraint set equals H; generator extraction is excluded.
Reconstruction consumes a supplied positive integer M and uses independent fresh sampling executions. For |G|=1 it returns the empty list without oracle calls.

Named oracle queries, ordinary gates, measurement, discarding, classical output, confidence preprocessing and circuit generation are separate cost coordinates. Exactly M hiding queries requires preparation and QFT circuits to make no hiding-oracle accesses.

load_bearing.statement: For every finite abelian hidden-subgroup instance with hidden subgroup H≤G, one execution of the exact sample procedure returns a valid character code with probability one. Each χ∈H⊥ has probability 1/|H⊥|=|H|/|G|, every character outside H⊥ has probability zero, and every invalid b-bit code has probability zero.

The input supplies explicit invariant-factor coordinates, an injectively encoded hiding function satisfying F(g)=F(g′) iff g−g′∈H, and a total Boolean extension for coherent XOR access. Output is a finite character-label list denoting the common kernel; success means that kernel equals H.

Let G be a finite abelian group, and let H⊊K≤G. Choose a character χ uniformly from H⊥. Then P(χ restricted to K is nontrivial)≥1/2. For every such outcome, K∩ker χ contains H and has index at least two in K.
For the stated independent common-kernel process with |G|=N≥2 and H≤K₀≤G, put s=ceil(log₂N) and M=ceil(4s+16 ln(1/δ)), where 0<δ<1. Then P(K_M≠H)≤δ. If H=K₀, failure probability is zero.

Starting with the uniform group state, evaluating an exact hiding oracle into a fresh output register and discarding that register gives ρ_G=(h/N)Σ_C |C⟩⟨C|, where the sum ranges over distinct H-cosets and |C⟩=h^(−1/2)Σ_{g∈C}|g⟩.
The common-kernel output always denotes a subgroup containing H. For |G|=1 it equals H=G without queries. For |G|≥2 and M=ceil(4 ceil(log₂|G|)+16 ln(1/δ)), it equals H with probability at least 1−δ.

published_dependencies.used_for: Character homomorphism, identity and inverse laws in the restriction-cut argument.
Subgroup closure, identity membership, and nonemptiness in common-kernel recovery.
The independent Binomial(M,1/2) lower-tail bound with deviation parameter 1/2, after the locally proved adaptive coupling.
Nonnegativity of coset-state and transformed rank-one density operators.
Computing density normalization and projective-measurement weights in encoded orthonormal coordinates.
Finite-mixture trace normalization and averaging the identical per-coset measurement distributions.

seams_checked.note: The cost theorem preserves the supplier's separate query, gate, generation and classical-cost coordinates; it does not infer uniformity or BQP membership from supplied exact circuits.
Checked character labels, negative-character normalization, normalized coset amplitudes, annihilator cardinality and double annihilation against the actual supplier statements and arguments.
Outer products and coordinate matrices respect the root linear-first pairing and the reversed Dirac pairing.
The supplied total XOR oracle and its explicit-circuit alternative retain separate access and implementation charges; no controlled access is inferred.
Encoded basis orthonormality, big-endian ordering, empty registers and contraction of equal output indices match the suppliers.
The full computational-basis projective measurement uses tr(ρP); invalid labels have zero weight because the transformed state is supported on valid codes.
Preparation, oracle and QFT are composed chronologically as supplied operations; discarding and terminal readout are explicit and separately costed.
The coset mixture and transformed rank-one operators have unit trace and nonnegative quadratic forms on positive-dimensional encoded registers, including zero-qubit registers.

The discrete-log consumer supplies exact preparation, full-register QFT and coherent function access on Z_q². Its fiber subgroup is generated by (−a,1); uniform annihilator sampling gives d=ac modulo q and uniform c, without a primality assumption.
